object.value: ordinary clothing can include a linen shirt and a woollen outer layer, with material and layers chosen for season, work and means
a belt can gather working clothes for movement; additional layers can be added in cold weather while work clothing still protects from dirt, weather, sparks or rough material
leather footwear can be repaired and dried after wet use; excessive heat can damage it, while wet ground, cold, walking and task hazards affect its use
a leather or coarse-cloth apron can protect main clothing during repeatedly dirty work; leather is particularly suitable around forge work
clothes for a feast or visit can be cleaner, less worn and less work-suited than everyday clothing
ironworking can require a forge and bellows for controlled working heat
a smith can use an anvil, hammer and tongs to hold and shape heated iron
iron stock and fuel can limit or delay a smith's current order
forge work can leave scale, ash, charcoal residue and small iron offcuts
a forge needs space where heat, smoke, fuel and fire risk can be managed
a carpenter can work timber with an axe, adze, chisel and marking tools, leaving shavings and offcuts
weaving can depend on yarn and a loom or setup that keeps warp under tension while weft is interlaced; the work can be paused and resumed
fishing can require water access and a suitable set of gear such as a net with floats and sinkers, lines, a trap basket or a boat, chosen by place and means
a master's working orders can include repairs and new tools; payment or exchange, and a craft worker's means, vary with orders, season, material costs and household obligations
a household can need shelter, heat, food preparation, storage and repair
maintaining clothing, tools and shelter can take priority over new goods
a master can hold responsibility for quality, tools, orders and instruction while means remain variable
a hired or dependent worker can control less of tools, time and output; treatment remains contextual
a learner can combine instruction with ordinary assistance and depend on a household or workshop
occupation or status can shape expectations without proving present wealth, stock or influence
visible conduct, reliability and reports can affect public reputation, with contextual effect
people can express requests, disagreement, deference or generosity differently in public and private

help can create gratitude, negotiation or reciprocal expectation rather than guaranteed debt
private needs such as care, food, rest, repair or household duty can shape choices without public proof
